Though the matter is listed for admission, with the consent of both parties, it is taken up for final disposal.

3. The present appeal is filed challenging the validity of the judgment and award passed in MVC No.207/2014 dated 26.12.2016 on the file of V Additional District and Sessions Judge and Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Belagavi.

entities.text: Additional District and Sessions Judge and Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Belagavi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
4. Facts in brief which are utmost necessary for disposal of this case are as under:
4.1 A claim petition came to be filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act in respect of accidental death of Sri.Abhijit Vithal Pawar in a road traffic accident that took place on 15.08.2012.

The claimants being the dependants NC:
2024:KHC-D:1110 of deceased contended that Sri.Abhijit Vithal Pawar was returning in a Mahindra goods vehicle bearing No.MH- 11/T-8269 after meeting his relatives in Dharwad.
Sri.Abhijit Vithal Pawar was driving the vehicle in a moderate speed by following all necessary traffic rules.
At that juncture, he had parked the vehicle and got down of the vehicle to attend the nature call.

At that juncture, motorcycle bearing No.KA-49/L-2892 came in a rash and negligent manner from Hattaragi side in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against him, whereby he sustained grievous injuries and died on the spot.
The claimants therefore laid a claim for awarding appropriate compensation.
4.2 In pursuance of the notices issued, respondents appeared before the Tribunal.
The first respondent died and his legal representatives were brought on record.
The first respondent during his lifetime, filed objection statement denying the entire claim petition averments.
Second respondent also filed objections denying the case of the claimants in toto.

4.3 The Tribunal after raising necessary issues and in view of the contentions of the parties,
recorded the evidence of Smt.Kanchan wife of the deceased as PW.1 and considered nine documentary evidence placed on record vide Exs.P.1 to P.9 and also evidence of Sri.Santosh L Nirwani, officer of the Insurance Company and considered Ex.R.1 which is the insurance policy in a pragmatic manner and allowed the claim petition in part and awarded compensation in a sum of Rs.15,03,000/- with interest at 9% per annum from the date of petition till recovery.

Sri. Basavaraj S/O Ningappa Patil vs Smt. Kanchan W/O Vijas Bhosale on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196438533/
3 4.4

entities.text: Ningappa Patil vs Smt. Kanchan W/O Vijas Bhosale
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Tribunal further fastened the liability on the owner of the motorcycle on the ground that the rider of motorcycle did not possess valid driving licence and exonerated the Insurance Company from liability.

5. Being aggrieved by the said judgment and award in exonerating the Insurance Company of the NC: 2024:KHC-D:1110 motorcycle and fastening liability on the owner of the motorcycle, one of the legal representatives of the owner of the motorcycle has preferred the present appeal.

6. Sri.S.S.Yaligar, learned counsel for the appellant reiterating the grounds urged in the appeal memorandum, contended that exonerating the Insurance Company on the ground that the rider of the motorcycle did not possess proper driving licence is incorrect and sought for allowing the appeal.
7. Alternatively, he contended that the Insurance Company be directed to pay compensation at the first instance and recover the same from the owner.
8. Per contra, Sri.Mallikarjun Madanalli contended that if the rider did not possess driving licence at all, question of fastening of liability on the Insurance Company would not arise at all.

On the same logic, Insurance Company cannot also be directed to pay compensation at the first instance and allow to recover the same from the NC: 2024:KHC-D:1110 owner of the motorcycle is also incorrect and sought for dismissal of the appeal.
9. In view of the rival contentions of the parties, this Court perused the material on record meticulously.
10. On such perusal, it is crystal clear that the charge sheet came to be filed against the rider of the motorcycle including provision of Motor Vehicles Act for not holding proper driving licence.
11. The material available on record has been rightly appreciated and compensation has been adjudged in a sum of Rs.15,03,000/-.
Therefore, there is no scope for reassessment of quantum of compensation.

12. Further, since the rider of motorcycle did not possess valid driving licence, the Tribunal has rightly appreciated the legal position and 25% contributory negligence is also attributed to the deceased himself in not taking proper precaution while getting down from Mahindra goods vehicle bearing No.MH-11/T-8269 for NC: 2024:KHC-D:1110 attending nature call.
Therefore, there is no scope for shifting the liability fastened on the owner to the Insurance Company.

13. The contentions therefore urged on behalf of the appellant cannot be countenanced in law inasmuch as the rider of the motorcycle has also been prosecuted for not possessing proper driving licence at the time of accident.

Since the rider of the motorcycle did not possess valid driving licence,
question of fastening liability on the Insurance Company or even to ordering for payment of compensation at the first instance and recover the same from the owner would not also arise.

Sri. Basavaraj S/O Ningappa Patil vs Smt. Kanchan W/O Vijas Bhosale on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196438533/
4 14.

sentences.text: Accordingly, this Court is of the considered opinion that none of the grounds urged in the appeal hold merit so as to interfere with the well reasoned order of the Tribunal which is impugned in the present appeal.

15. In view of the foregoing discussion, following order is passed:
NC: 2024:KHC-D:1110 ORDER (i) Appeal is meritless and is hereby dismissed.
(ii) Amount in deposit, if any, is ordered to be transmitted to the concerned Tribunal forthwith for disbursement.
(iii) Balance amount, if any, is to be deposited within six weeks from today.
